item.title: School Board Leaders Reelected - New Haven Independent
item.description: As Board of Ed keeps Yarborough, Wilcox, and Joyner in charge.

item.title: $113M Overhaul Planned For State St. Station, Court St. Bridge - New Haven Independent
item.description: The state plans to invest more than $100 million in a project designed to modernize -- and attract more travelers to -- the State Street train station, prompting neighbors to push for details on a related effort to convert the adjacent Court Street bridge to pedestrian and bicycle use, only.

item.title: "Inappropriate" Texts Lead To Teacher's Arrest - New Haven Independent
item.description: On one misdemeanor count of harmful communication with a minor.

item.title: Start-Up City Campaign Launched - New Haven Independent
item.description: New Haven is starting 2026 with a civic resolution: to become a "city of yes" for small-business start-ups. That's the goal of a new campaign called "Best City to Start."

item.title: Facing Accessibility Critique, State Closes Bus Ticket Sales Outlet's Door - New Haven Independent
item.description: All customers -- not just those in wheelchairs -- now have to wait outside to be helped at the new bus ticket sales outlet on Church Street, as the state works to make the one-step-elevated storefront "accessible for all.” The city’s disability commission, meanwhile, hosted a wide-ranging discussion about how the outlet’s accessibility problems extend beyond its lack of a ramp.

item.title: School Board OKs Teachers Union Contract - New Haven Independent
item.description: Teeing the 3-year deal up for Board of Alders review.

item.title: Faith Matters: Divine Light In Times Of Darkness - New Haven Independent
Artists Go With The Flow
item.description: In latest Kehler Liddell group show.

item.title: Zoners Reject Sports Club Plan For Industrial Lot - New Haven Independent
item.description: In a divided vote, the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) denied a use variance that would have paved the way for an outdoor soccer field, a volleyball court, and a concession stand to be built on a vacant industrial Fair Haven lot. Now, the lot's owners are considering putting a construction business there instead.

item.title: Republican Alder-Hopeful To Run In Contested Special Election - New Haven Independent
item.description: Kyle Ross was tapped this week to become the new co-chair of Ward 7's Republican Town Committee. He also has his eyes on another political seat: East Rock/Downtown alder.
